questions.stem: For this part , you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay titled“Are people becoming addicted to technology?”.The statement given below is for your reference. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words. Numerous studies claim that addiction to technology is real and it has the same effect on the brain as drug addiction.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
Are people becoming addicted to technology? My answer is a definite yes. As numerous studies claim that addiction to technology is real, this problem deserves our serious attention.

Signs of such addiction are everywhere in daily life. Many people check their smartphones the moment they wake up and keep scrolling short videos until midnight. While technology is designed to make life easier, an increasing number of us feel anxious once we are separated from our screens. As a result, real conversations, sleep and study are all disturbed, which shows that our reliance has quietly turned into dependence.

In my view, therefore, people are indeed getting hooked on technology. However, this does not mean we should abandon it. What matters is to use technology in a rational way, setting limits on screen time and leaving room for the real world.

transcript.text: And finally in tonight's news, a 9-year-old boy named Joe, told not to draw in class, wins a job decorating a restaurant with his drawings. Rather than shutting down the habit of drawing in his school's workbook, Joe's parents decided to encourage his creativity by sending their son to an after-school art class. His teacher recognized Joe's talent and posted all his work online, which led to something pretty wonderful.
transcript.zh: 最后是今晚的新闻，一名9岁男孩Joe在课堂上被禁止画画，却凭借自己的画作赢得了一份装饰餐厅的工作。Joe的父母没有制止他在学校作业本上画画的习惯，而是决定鼓励他的创造力，送他去参加课后艺术班。他的老师认可了Joe的天赋，并把他所有的作品发布到网上，这带来了一件非常美好的事情。

transcript.text: A restaurant named "Number 4" in Newcastle contacted Joe's teacher to ask if the 9-year-old could come and decorate its dining-room with his drawings. Every day after school, Joe's dad drives him to the restaurant so he can put his ideas straight on the wall. Once he's all done, the work will remain there permanently.
transcript.zh: Newcastle一家名为"Number 4"的餐厅联系了Joe的老师，询问这个9岁的孩子能否来用他的画作装饰餐厅的用餐区。每天放学后，Joe的爸爸开车送他去餐厅，这样他就可以把自己的创意直接画在墙上。一旦全部完成，这些作品将永久保留在那里。

transcript.text: Joe's dad said Joe is a really talented little boy. He's excellent at school. He's great at football. But drawing is definitely what he is most passionate about.
transcript.zh: Joe的爸爸说Joe是一个非常有天赋的小男孩。他在学校表现出色。他足球踢得很好。但画画绝对是他最热爱的事情。

questions.stem: What did Joe's parents decide to do?

options.text: Enrol him in a Newcastle football club.
Send him to an after-school art class.
Forbid him to draw in his workbook.
Help him post his drawings online.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Rather than shutting down the habit of drawing in his school's workbook, Joe's parents decided to encourage his creativity by sending their son to an after-school art class.信号：Rather than后的转折落点 。答案信号是句首的 Rather than shutting down the habit of drawing——"而不是去扼杀"。Rather than 是一个含蓄否定的转折标…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 说"给他报名 Newcastle 足球俱乐部"。录音确实念到了 He's great at football. 和地名 Newcastle，但那是第3段描述乔"球踢得好"，第2段 Newcastle 是餐厅所在地，根本没有"父母给他报足球队"这回事。它把零散原词拼成了假事件。 借用原文：shutting down the habit of drawing in his school's workbook
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：C 说"禁止他在练习册上画画"。录音里 shutting down the habit of drawing in his school's workbook 确实提到"扼杀在练习册上画画的习惯"，但它前面有 Rather than——是父母"没有"做的事。C 恰恰取了被转折否定掉的那半句，方向反了。 借用原文：His teacher recognized Joe's talent and posted all his work online
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：D 说"帮他把画发到网上"。录音里 His teacher recognized Joe's talent and posted all his work online 确实有"发到网上"，但做这件事的是"老师"，不是"父母"。题问的是父母，把老师的行为安到父母头上，张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（sending their son to an after-school art class ↔ Send him to an after-school art class. 几乎原句对应）

optionAnalysis.B: 过度推断：B 说"雇佣乔粉刷其建筑的所有墙面"。录音确实有 put his ideas straight on the wall（把想法画到墙上），但 B 把它夸成 paint all the walls（所有墙），还说成 Hired（雇佣、含付薪），录音只说 contacted...to ask（联系询问），既没说付钱雇佣、也没说所有墙面。 借用原文：decorate its dining-room
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：C 说"翻新了厨房和所有的用餐区"。录音说的是 decorate its dining-room——装饰"用餐区"，C 一是把 decorate（用画装饰）偷换成 Renovated（整体翻新装修），二是凭空加了 kitchen（厨房）和 all（所有），范围和动作都被放大，录音都没说。 借用原文：posted all his work online
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 说"请求乔授权使用他网上的画"。录音里 posted all his work online 确有"发到网上"，但那是老师发画的动作，餐厅这边只是 contacted Joe's teacher to ask if the 9-year-old could come——请人来现场画，根本没有"求授权用网上的画"这回事。online 是被挪用的原词。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（contacted Joe's teacher to ask if the 9-year-old could come and decorate its dining-room ↔ Contacted Joe to decorate its dining-room. concise概括对应）

questions.stem: What is Kirsteen Marshall trying to do?

options.text: Identify the suspect on the security video.
Beg for help from the police.
Post pictures of her pet dog on social media.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Kirsteen Marshall, a 34-year-old mum of one, posted a tearful video on social media Wednesday, begging for the safe return of her beloved pet dog.信号：begging 点出真实目的 。这一句里 begging for the safe return of her beloved pet dog 是表意图的动词短语，直接道出她做这一切的根本目的，是承载答案的信号句；前…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音确实说她 posted an image of a man suspected of stealing the dog，B 盗用了这里的 suspect 原词，但发嫌疑人照片是她找狗路上的一个中间手段，不是她『努力要达成』的目的，答非所问。 借用原文：Police are investigating the incident.
optionAnalysis.C: 答非所问：录音末尾只说 Police are investigating the incident.，是警方在查案，并没有说她去『乞求警方帮忙』；C 把警方的存在偷换成她的诉求，与题干问的『她想做什么』错位。 借用原文：posted a tearful video on social media Wednesday
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：录音说她 posted a tearful video on social media，D 盗用 social media、post 原词，但发社交媒体只是她为找回狗采取的途径，跟 B 一样是手段而非她要达成的目的。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（begging for the safe return of her beloved pet dog ↔ Get her pet dog back 求平安归来=把狗找回）

questions.stem: What does the news report say about Kirsteen Marshall's family?

options.text: It is suffering a great deal from the incident.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：The family is now offering a £5,000 reward for the safe return of the dog after launching a social media campaign to find the thief.信号：family+具体金额坐实 。这一句以题干主语 The family 起头，并给出具体金额 offering a £5,000 reward，主语对上、又带数字，正是承载答案的信号句；预读时圈的 reward 在此被…

optionAnalysis.A: 过度推断：录音第一段说她发了 a tearful video（含泪视频），A 据此推出全家『受了很大煎熬』，但报道只描述了行动（发视频、悬赏），并未陈述家人正承受痛苦这一事实，属于在原文情绪线索上推过了头。 借用原文：Police are investigating the incident.
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：录音说 Police are investigating the incident.，是警方在调查；B 盗用 police、investigation 原词，却把『警方查案』安到了家人头上，张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：全篇只讲发视频、贴嫌疑人照片、悬赏、警方调查，从没说过把案子告上 local district court；C 是录音里完全没有依据的动作，属凭空添加。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（offering a £5,000 reward for the safe return of the dog ↔ offering a big reward to anyone who helps 5000镑=一大笔悬赏）

transcript.text: London's Eggs & Bread café offers boiled eggs, toast, jam, and bacon, as well as tea, coffee and orange juice. But at the end of the meal, customers don't have to worry about the bill. Hungry customers can pay whatever amount they can afford to eat at the café, or nothing at all.
transcript.zh: 伦敦的Eggs & Bread咖啡馆提供煮鸡蛋、吐司、果酱和培根,以及茶、咖啡和橙汁。但在用餐结束时,顾客不必担心账单。饥饿的顾客可以支付他们能承受的任何金额在这家咖啡馆用餐,或者什么都不付。

transcript.text: Owner Guy Wilson says his café aims to build community, rather than profits. He wants to provide a bridge for people to connect in an area that has been divided by class and wealth by providing affordable breakfasts.
transcript.zh: 店主Guy Wilson说,他的咖啡馆旨在建立社区,而非追求利润。他希望通过提供人们负担得起的早餐,为这个被阶级和财富分割的地区的人们搭建一座连接的桥梁。

transcript.text: The café is open in the mornings every day of the year and has two members of staff or supervisors on shift every day. The café doesn't use volunteers, but pays its staff to ensure consistency in its service. It doesn't take donations and doesn't want to be seen as a charity.
transcript.zh: 这家咖啡馆全年每天早上营业,每天有两名员工或主管值班。咖啡馆不使用志愿者,而是支付员工工资以确保服务的一致性。它不接受捐赠,也不希望被视为慈善机构。

transcript.text: Mr. Wilson says, when people start to know other people around them, they realize they're not that different. And whatever their financial background, or their educational background, most people will have something in common with each other. He says it's important that his café can offer his customers security and permanence.
transcript.zh: Wilson先生说,当人们开始了解周围的其他人时,他们会意识到彼此并没有那么不同。无论他们的经济背景或教育背景如何,大多数人都会与彼此有一些共同点。他说,他的咖啡馆能够为顾客提供安全感和稳定性是很重要的。

questions.stem: What does Guy Wilson say his café aims to do?

options.text: Provide free meals to the local poor.
Help people connect with each other.
Help eliminate class difference in his area.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：Owner Guy Wilson says his café aims to build community, rather than profits. He wants to provide a bridge for people to connect in an area that has been divided by class and wealth by providing affordable breakfasts.信号：表目的的 aims to / wants to 。这句里 aims to build community和 wants to provide a bridge for people to connect接连出现两个表…

optionAnalysis.A: 偷换概念：原文说店主靠 providing affordable breakfasts（提供负担得起的早餐）来搭桥，affordable 是"付得起、便宜"，并不等于 free（免费）；A 把"affordable"夸大成 free meals，又添了"the local poor（当地穷人）"这个原文没指明的对象，是听到"早餐"就误选的陷阱。 借用原文：has been divided by class and wealth
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：原文只说该地区 has been divided by class and wealth（被阶层和财富所割裂），店是想在这种环境里"搭桥连接"，从没说要 eliminate（消除）阶层差异。C 盗用了 class 这个原词，再把"搭桥"夸大成"消除差异"——听到 class 就选它正中陷阱。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：原文明确老板要的是 build community, rather than profits（营造社区而非利润），目标根本不在"服务档次"上；D 的 first-class service（一流服务）属于无中生有，还隐隐与"不追求利润"的取向相反，是用一个听起来"高大上"的褒义短语来诱选。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（provide a bridge for people to connect ↔ Help people connect with each other. 搭桥让人连接=帮人互相连接）

questions.stem: What does the news report say about Eggs & Bread café?

options.text: It does not supervise its employees.
It donates regularly to a local charity.
It is open round the clock.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：The café doesn't use volunteers, but pays its staff to ensure consistency in its service.信号：否定 doesn't + 转折 but 。答案句靠 doesn't use volunteers这个明确否定，加上 but pays its staff的转折点出真意——"不用义工、改用付薪员工"。否定词与转折词同现…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：原文说店 has two members of staff or supervisors on shift every day（每天有两名员工或主管值班），明明是"有人盯班、管得到"；A 盗用 supervisors / staff 这层意思却反过来说 does not supervise its employees（不监管员工），与原文相反，是听到"supervisor"就误选的陷阱。 借用原文：doesn't take donations and doesn't want to be seen as a charity
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：原文说店 doesn't take donations and doesn't want to be seen as a charity（不接受捐款、也不想被当成慈善机构）；B 盗用 donations / charity 两个原词，却说成 donates regularly to a local charity（定期向当地慈善机构捐款），方向完全反了——这是"听到 charity 就选"的高诱惑陷阱。 借用原文：is open in the mornings every day of the year
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：原文说店 is open in the mornings every day of the year（一年中每天早上营业）；D 的 open round the clock 是"24 小时全天候"，把"每天早上"夸大成"全天不打烊"，是听到 open every day 就误选的时间细节陷阱。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（doesn't use volunteers ↔ It does not use volunteers. doesn't=does not，几乎原句）

questions.stem: What happens when people start to know each other according to Guy Wilson?

options.text: They will realise the importance of communication.
They will come to the café even more frequently.
They will care less about their own background.
They will find they have something in common.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：Mr. Wilson says, when people start to know other people around them, they realize they're not that different. And whatever their financial background, or their educational background, most people will have something in common with each other.信号：条件 when + 结果 they realize / will have 。答案句以 when people start to know other people around them起头，后面 they rea…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：原文老板谈的是人们会 realize they're not that different（意识到彼此没那么不同），从没说他们会意识到 communication（沟通）的重要性；A 的"沟通"是原文没有的概念，属凭"咖啡馆=交流"的常识补出来的项。
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：café 一词录音里反复出现，B 的 come to the café even more frequently（更频繁地来店）就借这个原词诱选；但原文谈的是人熟了之后"意识到彼此相似"，根本没说人们会更常来，属听到 café 就选的答非所问。 借用原文：whatever their financial background, or their educational background, most people will have something in common
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：原文说 whatever their financial background, or their educational background, most people will have something in common（无论何种背景，大多有共同点）；C 盗用 background 原词，却把结论换成 care less about their own background（更少在意自己的背景）——原文讲"有共同点"，不是讲"在意程度变低"，是 D 的近义干扰项。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（most people will have something in common with each other ↔ They will find they have something in common. have something in common 原样保留）

transcript.text: M: So what time do you think we should have the party on Saturday?
transcript.zh: M: 那你觉得我们星期六的聚会应该定在什么时候？

transcript.text: W: How about inviting people to come at 6:00 p.m.? Then we'll have the afternoon to prepare food and drink, and stuff like that.

transcript.text: M: Yes, I was thinking that around 6:00 would be good too. What food should we provide?
transcript.zh: M: 是的,我也在想6点左右比较好。我们应该准备什么食物？

transcript.text: 1 Pigs are not native to North America.
They were first introduced to California by Spanish and Russian explorers and settlers many centuries ago.
In the early times, pigs were allowed to wander freely in search of food.

This practice also allowed many pigs to escape from farms and live in the wild, which became a problem. 2 In fact, as one of the most damaging invasive species on the continent, wild pigs cause millions of dollars in crop damage yearly.
They also harbor dozens of diseases that threaten both humans and farm animals.
Forest patches with wild pigs have been found to have considerably reduced plant and animal diversity.
In addition to either eating other animals or their food supply, wild pigs damage native habitats by rooting up grasses and rubbing on trees.
Their activities may also create opportunities for invasive plants to colonize these areas.
Wild pigs will eat almost anything containing calories.
Mice, deer, birds, snakes and frogs are among their victims.
They can also harm other wild species through indirect competition, rather than eating them or shrinking their food supply.
On one particular United States island, wild pigs themselves became an attractive food source for a species of mainland eagle.
The eagles began breeding on the island, and also feeding on a species of native fox.
The foxes were almost wiped out completely.

transcript.text: A pair of entrepreneurs are planning to build and launch a spacecraft that would carry and roast coffee beans in outer space.
transcript.zh: 一对创业者正计划建造并发射一艘航天器，用于在外太空中携带并烘焙咖啡豆。

transcript.text: The craft will use the heat of re-entry to roast coffee beans as they float inside it in a pressurised tank. The effect would be to roast the beans all over, and produce perfect coffee. The businessmen say that on Earth, beans can easily break apart and get burned in the roaster. transcript.text: The spacecraft will reach a height of around 200 km. The beans would then be roasted in the heat generated by the craft's 20-minute re-entry into Earth's atmosphere. Temperatures in the pressurised tank will be kept to around 200℃.
transcript.zh: 航天器将到达约200公里的高度。随后咖啡豆将在航天器重返地球大气层的20分钟过程中,利用产生的热量进行烘焙。加压舱内的温度将保持在200℃左右。

transcript.text: Once back on Earth, the planet's first space-roasted beans would be used to make coffee that would be sold for the first time in Dubai. This is where the pair's company is based. It is not clear how much they would charge for a cup.

transcript.text: Surprisingly, the Space Roaster concept—should it go ahead—will not be the first attempt to take coffee into space. In 2015, two Italian companies collaborated on the construction of a similar type of spacecraft, which was the first coffee machine designed for use in space.

transcript.text: In cold and snowy Alaska, there's a village called Takotna. It has a population of a mere 49 souls. Each March, this tiny village swells up in numbers, because it is located in the middle of a race that takes place every year. It is a seven-day race, called the Iditarod Trail, and participants stop at Takotna for their obligatory 24-hour rest. Lucky for them, Takotna is famous for its delicious fruit pies.
transcript.zh: 在寒冷多雪的阿拉斯加，有一个名叫Takotna的村庄。它的人口仅有49人。每年三月，这个小村庄的人数会激增，因为它位于一年一度举行的比赛路线中途。这是一场为期七天的比赛，名为Iditarod Trail，参赛者会在Takotna停留进行规定的24小时休息。对他们来说幸运的是，Takotna以其美味的水果派而闻名。

transcript.text: Weeks before the competitors arrive, the residents of Takotna start preparing for what is without question their biggest event of the year. The whole village chips in to help, including the kids, who end up developing their baking skills at an early age. The exhausted and hungry racers are greeted with delightful pies of all kinds, such as apple, orange, lemon or banana. They consume the pies as stomach warming race fuel. The toughness of the race allows for racers to eat pretty much whatever they want. The more calories, the better.
transcript.zh: 在参赛者到来前几周，Takotna的居民就开始为这场毫无疑问是他们全年最盛大的活动做准备。全村人都参与帮忙，包括孩子们，他们因此在很小的时候就开始培养烘焙技能。筋疲力尽且饥肠辘辘的参赛者会受到各种美味派的款待，比如苹果派、橙子派、柠檬派或香蕉派。他们将这些派作为暖胃的比赛燃料来食用。比赛的艰苦程度使得参赛者几乎可以想吃什么就吃什么。卡路里越高越好。

transcript.text: Takotna has gained a reputation for its dessert-based hospitality since the 1970s. It started with one person, Jan Newton. Jan moved from Idaho with her husband in 1972 and opened a restaurant. Her rich and filling-fruit pies quickly got the racers' attention, and the village gained some fame as a result. Proud residents then started to refer to Jan as Queen of Takotna.
transcript.zh: 自20世纪70年代以来，Takotna因其以甜点为特色的热情好客而声名远扬。这一切始于一个人，Jan Newton。Jan和她的丈夫在1972年从Idaho搬来，并开了一家餐厅。她制作的香浓饱腹的水果派很快引起了参赛者的注意，村庄也因此获得了一些名气。自豪的居民随后开始称Jan为Takotna女王。

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：It is the best time for sightseeing. 说三月是观光最佳时节，但录音只讲了比赛带来人流，全程没提观光或景色好坏，属凭常识脑补出来的理由。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: This month, more than 4 million students across the nation will begin high school. Many will do well. But many will not. Consider that nearly two-thirds of students will experience the "ninth-grade shock," which refers to a dramatic drop in a student's academic performance. Some students cope with this shock by avoiding challenges. For instance, they may drop difficult coursework. Others may experience a hopelessness that results in failing their core classes, such as English, science and math.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: This should matter a great deal to parents, teachers and policymakers. Ultimately it should matter to the students themselves and society at large, because students' experience of transitioning(过渡) to the ninth grade can have long-term consequences not only for the students themselves but for their home communities. We make these observations as research psychologists who have studied how schools and families can help young people thrive.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: In the new global economy, students who fail to finish the ninth grade with passing grades in college preparatory coursework are very unlikely to graduate on time and go on to get jobs. One study has calculated that the lifetime benefit to the local economy for a single additional student who completes high school is half a million dollars or more. This is based on higher earnings and avoided costs in health care, crime, welfare dependence and other things.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The consequences of doing poorly in the ninth grade can impact more than students' ability to find a good job. It can also impact the extent to which they enjoy life. Students lose many of the friends they turned to for support when they move from the eighth to the ninth grade. One study of ninth-grade students found that 50 percent of friendships among ninth graders changed from one month to the next, signaling striking instability in friendships.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: In addition, studies find the first year of high school typically shows one of the greatest increases in depression of any year over the lifespan. Researchers think that one explanation is that ties to friends are broken while academic demands are rising. Furthermore, most adult cases of clinical depression first emerge in adolescence(青春期). The World Health Organization reports that depression has the greatest burden of disease worldwide, in terms of the total cost of treatment and the loss of productivity.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Given all that's riding on having a successful ninth grade experience, it pays to explore what can be done to meet the academic, social and emotional challenges of the transition to high school. So far, our studies have yielded one main insight: Students' beliefs about change—their beliefs about whether people are stuck one way forever, or whether people can change their personalities and abilities—are related to their ability to cope, succeed academically and maintain good mental health. Past research has called these beliefs "mindsets(思维模式)," with a "fixed mindset" referring to the belief that people cannot change and a "growth mindset" referring to the belief that people can change.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: In one recent study, we examined 360 adolescents' beliefs about the nature of "smartness"—that is, their fixed mindsets about intelligence. We then assessed biological stress responses for students whose grades were dropping by examining their stress hormones(荷尔蒙). Students who believed that intelligence is fixed—that you are stuck being "not smart" if you struggle in school—showed higher levels of stress hormones when their grades were declining at the beginning of the ninth grade. If students believed that intelligence could improve—that is to say, when they held more of a growth mindset of intelligence—they showed lower levels of stress hormones when their grades were declining. This was an exciting result because it showed that the body's stress responses are not determined solely by one's grades. Instead, declining grades only predicted worse stress hormones among students who believed that worsening grades were a permanent and hopeless state of affairs.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: We also investigated the social side of the high school transition. In this study, instead of teaching students that their smartness can change, we taught them that their social standing—that is, whether they are bullied or excluded or left out—can change over time. We then looked at high school students' stress responses to daily social difficulties. That is, we taught them a growth mindset about their social lives. In this study, students came into the laboratory and were asked to give a public speech in front of upper-year students. The topic of the speech was what makes one popular in high school. Following this, students had to complete a difficult mental math task in front of the same upper-year students.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Experiment results showed that students who were not taught that people can change showed poor stress responses. When these students gave the speech, their blood vessels contracted and their hearts pumped less blood through the body—both responses that the body shows when it is preparing for damage or defeat after a physical threat. Then they gave worse speeches and made more mistakes in math. But when students were taught that people can change, they had better responses to stress, in part because they felt like they had the resources to deal with the demanding situation. Students who got the growth mindset intervention(干预) showed less-contracted blood vessels and their hearts pumped more blood—both of which contributed to more oxygen getting to the brain, and, ultimately, better performance on the speech and mental math tasks.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: These findings lead to several possibilities that we are investigating further. First, we are working to replicate(复制) these findings in more diverse school communities. We want to know in which types of schools and for which kinds of students these growth mindset ideas help young people adapt to the challenges of high school. We also hope to learn how teachers, parents or school counselors can help students keep their ongoing academic or social difficulties in perspective. We wonder what would happen if schools helped to make beliefs about the potential for change and improvement a larger feature of the overall school culture, especially for students starting the ninth grade.

paragraphs.text: Focusing on STEM skills is important, but the reality is that STEM skills are enhanced and more relevant when combined with traditional, hands-on creative activities. This combination is proving to be the best way to prepare today's children to be the makers and builders of tomorrow. That is why technology companies are partnering with educators to bring back good, old-fashioned play.

These are skills acquired when kids tinker(鼓捣小玩意). High-tech industries such as NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory have found that their best overall problem solvers were master tinkerers in their youth.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: There are cognitive(认知的) benefits of doing things the way we did as children—building something, tearing it down, then building it up again. Research shows that given 15 minutes of free play, four- and five-year-olds will spend a third of this time engaged in spatial, mathematical, and architectural activities. This type of play—especially with building blocks—helps children discover and develop key principles in math and geometry.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: If play and building are critical to 21st-century skill development, that's really good news for two reasons: Children are born builders, makers, and creators, so fostering(培养) 21st-century skills may be as simple as giving kids room to play, tinker and try things out, even as they grow older. Secondly, it doesn't take 21st-century technology to foster 21st-century skills. This is especially important for under-resourced schools and communities. Taking whatever materials are handy and tinkering with them is a simple way to engage those important "maker" skills. And anyone, anywhere, can do it.
